exercises.name: intro1
exercises.hint: This one is already correct. Delete the `// I AM NOT DONE` comment at the top of the file, save, and clings will move on.

exercises.name: intro2
exercises.hint: C23 sets `__STDC_VERSION__` to `202311L`. Compile with `-std=c23` (clings already does). Fill in that number so the static_assert holds.

exercises.name: bool1
exercises.hint: C23 makes `bool`, `true`, and `false` keywords. You no longer need `<stdbool.h>` macros or `_Bool`. Write `bool ready = true;`.

exercises.name: bool2
exercises.hint: Give `is_even` the return type `bool` and return `true` or `false`. `_Generic(true, bool: 1, default: 0)` is 1 in C23 — `true` is not an `int`.

exercises.name: nullptr1
exercises.hint: The C23 null pointer constant is the keyword `nullptr`. It is not `NULL`, not `0`, and not `(void *)0`. Assign `p = nullptr;`.

exercises.name: nullptr2
exercises.hint: `nullptr` has type `nullptr_t`, from `<stddef.h>`. Declare `nullptr_t np = nullptr;` and then assign that to any pointer type.

exercises.name: nullptr3
exercises.hint: `_Generic(nullptr, nullptr_t: 1, default: 0)` is 1. `_Generic(NULL, ...)` typically matches `void *` instead. Use `nullptr` in the `_Generic` selector.

exercises.name: literals1
exercises.hint: Binary integer literals use the `0b` or `0B` prefix: `0b1010` is 10, `0b1111'0000` is 240. Replace the placeholder with a binary literal equal to 42.

exercises.name: literals2
exercises.hint: C23 lets you put `'` between digits: `1'000'000`, `0xFF'FF`, `0b1010'0001`. The apostrophe is not a character and does not change the value.

exercises.name: literals3
exercises.hint: Write the permission bits as binary literals. `READ` is `0b100`, `WRITE` is `0b010`, `EXEC` is `0b001`. Then `READ | WRITE` is `0b110`.

exercises.name: auto1
exercises.hint: `auto` in C23 infers the type from the initializer: `auto n = 42;` is an `int`. Replace `???` with `auto`.

exercises.name: auto2
exercises.hint: `auto` without an initializer is invalid. Write `auto n = 42;` — inference needs a value to look at.

exercises.name: typeof1
exercises.hint: `typeof(expr)` is the type of that expression. `typeof(seed) copy = seed;` makes `copy` the same type as `seed` (here, `double`).

exercises.name: typeof2
exercises.hint: `typeof` keeps qualifiers; `typeof_unqual` strips `const`/`volatile`/`restrict`/`_Atomic`. Use `typeof_unqual(name)` so the copy is a plain `char[8]` you can write to. Actually it is an array type — use a pointer: `typeof_unqual(*name)` is `char`.

exercises.name: typeof3
exercises.hint: A type-generic swap: `#define SWAP(a, b) do { typeof(a) tmp = (a); (a) = (b); (b) = tmp; } while (0)`. `typeof(a)` gives you a temporary of the right type without naming it.

exercises.name: constexpr1
exercises.hint: `constexpr int n = 4;` is an integer constant expression. You can use `n` as an array length and in `static_assert`. Replace `const` with `constexpr`.

exercises.name: constexpr2
exercises.hint: In C, `const int n = 4;` is *not* an integer constant expression, so `static_assert(n == 4)` is illegal and `int a[n]` is a VLA. `constexpr` is the keyword that actually produces a compile-time constant. Change `const` to `constexpr`.

exercises.name: attr1
exercises.hint: `[[nodiscard]]` makes it a warning (an error here) to ignore the return value. Store it: `int code = must_check();` and use `code`.

exercises.name: attr2
exercises.hint: Mark things you intentionally do not use with `[[maybe_unused]]`. You can put it on the variable: `[[maybe_unused]] int scratch = 0;` and on a parameter.

exercises.name: attr3
exercises.hint: A `case` that falls into the next one needs `[[fallthrough]];` as a statement at the end of the case, just before the next `case` label.

exercises.name: attr4
exercises.hint: `old_api` is `[[deprecated]]`. Call `new_api` instead. The deprecation message on the old function tells you what to use.

exercises.name: init1
exercises.hint: C23 allows empty initializers: `T x = {};` zeroes `x`, including scalars, structs, and arrays. Replace the bogus initializer with `{}`.

exercises.name: func1
exercises.hint: C23 lets you omit a parameter name you do not use: `int callback(void *ctx, int /* unused */) {` can be `int callback(void *ctx, int) {`. Drop the dummy name.

exercises.name: func2
exercises.hint: C23 allows a variadic function with no named parameters: `int first(...)`. Then `va_start(ap)` takes only the `va_list` — there is no last named argument to pass.

exercises.name: enum1
exercises.hint: C23 enums may fix their underlying type: `enum color : unsigned char { Red, Green, Blue };`. Add `: uint8_t` (from `<stdint.h>`) so `sizeof` is 1.

exercises.name: enum2
exercises.hint: Without a fixed type, enumerators had to fit in `int`. Give the enum an underlying type wide enough, e.g. `enum : unsigned long { Big = 1UL << 32 };` or `uint64_t`.

exercises.name: bitint1
exercises.hint: Bit-precise integers are `_BitInt(N)` and `unsigned _BitInt(N)`. Declare `unsigned _BitInt(8) byte;` so the value 255 fits exactly in 8 bits.

exercises.name: bitint2
exercises.hint: Bit-precise suffixes are `wb` / `WB` for `_BitInt` and `uwb` / `UWB` for unsigned. `0b1111uwb` has type `unsigned _BitInt(4)`. Use a `uwb` literal.

exercises.name: bitint3
exercises.hint: `unsigned _BitInt(3)` is exactly 3 value bits, so it wraps modulo 8. `7uwb + 1uwb` is `0`. Declare the addends as `unsigned _BitInt(3)` (or `uwb` literals) so the wrap is visible.

exercises.name: align1
exercises.hint: `alignas` and `alignof` are keywords in C23 (the old `_Alignas` / `_Alignof` spellings still work). Write `alignas(32) unsigned char buf[64];` and compare with `alignof(buf)`.

exercises.name: labels1
exercises.hint: C23 allows a label before a declaration or a closing brace. You no longer need a null statement (`done:;`). Put `int n = 1;` immediately after `done:`.

exercises.name: pp1
exercises.hint: `#elifdef NAME` is `#elif defined(NAME)`, and `#elifndef NAME` is `#elif !defined(NAME)`. Use `#elifdef HAVE_C23` in the `#if` chain.

exercises.name: pp2
exercises.hint: `#embed "mascot.txt"` expands to a comma-separated list of byte values. Put it inside the array initializer: `unsigned char mascot[] = { #embed "mascot.txt" };`.

exercises.name: pp3
exercises.hint: `__has_include(<header.h>)` is 1 when the header can be included. Use it to take the branch that includes `<stdbit.h>`.

exercises.name: pp4
exercises.hint: `__VA_OPT__(x)` expands to `x` only when `__VA_ARGS__` is non-empty. For a log macro: `#define LOG(fmt, ...) printf(fmt __VA_OPT__(,) __VA_ARGS__)` so `LOG("hi\n")` does not get a trailing comma.

exercises.name: stdbit1
exercises.hint: Include `<stdbit.h>`. For an `unsigned char` value `0x10` (`0b00010000`): `stdc_count_ones` is 1, `stdc_leading_zeros` is 3, `stdc_trailing_zeros` is 4. The width is the width of the type, not of `unsigned int`.

exercises.name: stdbit2
exercises.hint: `stdc_has_single_bit(x)` is true for powers of two. `stdc_bit_floor` rounds down to a power of two, `stdc_bit_ceil` rounds up, `stdc_bit_width` is `floor(log2(x))+1` (and 0 for 0).

exercises.name: ckdint1
exercises.hint: Include `<stdckdint.h>`. `ckd_add(&result, a, b)` stores `a+b` in `*result` and returns `true` if the result does not fit in `result`'s type. Check the overflow of `INT_MAX + 1`.

exercises.name: ckdint2
exercises.hint: `ckd_mul` / `ckd_sub` work like `ckd_add`: `bool overflow = ckd_mul(&out, a, b);`. Use `ckd_mul` to detect that `100000 * 100000` does not fit in an `int`.

exercises.name: lib1
exercises.hint: `strdup` and `strndup` are standard in C23 (`<string.h>`). `char *copy = strdup(src);` allocates and copies. Free the copy when you are done.

exercises.name: lib2
exercises.hint: `unreachable()` in `<stddef.h>` tells the compiler a path cannot happen. Put it in the `default` of a switch you have already covered exhaustively. The C23 spelling is `unreachable();` — not `unreach()`.

exercises.name: compound1
exercises.hint: C23 lets a compound literal take a storage-class specifier. `(int[]){1,2,3}` has automatic storage and dies when the function returns. `(static int[]){1,2,3}` lives for the whole program, so returning its address is safe.

exercises.name: quiz1
exercises.hint: This one mixes several C23 features. Fill in: `auto`, `nullptr`, `bool`/`true`, a binary literal, `constexpr`, and `typeof`. The `static_assert`s and `assert`s tell you exactly which types and values are expected.
